title: Wide intervals come from too few honest programs
caption: One dot per pairwise comparison in MATCHED-FPR: how many honest programs sit above the shared cutoff, against the width of the 95% interval on the recall gap. The dashed line is this project's bar of five honest rows; the stepped line is the median at each count.
notes: The median interval runs 71.2 points wide when the cutoff rests on one honest row and 24.2 at five. Nothing about the monitors changes along this axis; only how much honest data the threshold was estimated from.
Data quality, which is the point of this figure: 93 of 104 comparisons rest on fewer than five honest rows, and only 11 of 104 separate from zero at all.
No comparison rests on exactly four honest rows, and none rests on more than five. The gaps are real, not missing data: a rung exists only where both monitors can serve the same rate exactly.

This figure used to reach 46 honest rows. That comparison, Sonnet against the Gemma 3 4B 0-100 arm, left the set when the parser-default repairs landed: one corrected honest score moved that arm's achievable rate and the shared rung disappeared. M09 and MATCHED-FPR record it.
Ported from the data explorer's e3-width-vs-rows view, reading the committed pairwise table.
